Document.title: Document
Document.description: Represents an uploaded document in the PDF Spark application, which can be processed by various tools.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Document entity.

originalFileName.description: The original name of the file as uploaded by the user.

storageReference.description: A URI reference to the document's location in the storage system (e.g., Firebase Storage).

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the uploaded file (e.g., 'application/pdf', 'image/jpeg').

fileSizeKB.description: The size of the document in kilobytes.

uploadTimestamp.description: The date and time when the document was uploaded.

status.description: The current processing status of the document (e.g., 'uploaded', 'processing', 'processed', 'failed').

AIResult.title: AIResult
AIResult.description: Stores the output generated by AI content analysis tools, which can be shared publicly.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AIResult entity.

documentId.description: Reference to the Document entity that this AI result was generated from. (Relationship: Document 1:N AIResult)

toolName.description: The name of the AI tool that generated this result (e.g., 'PDF Summarizer', 'Key Information Extractor').

generatedContent.description: The actual content generated by the AI tool, such as a summary or extracted information.

shareSlug.description: A unique, SEO-friendly slug used to construct the public URL for this result page.

createdAt.description: The date and time when this AI result was created.

isPubliclyShareable.description: A boolean flag indicating whether this AI result is enabled for public sharing.

definition.description: Stores user-uploaded private PDF documents. Authorization is path-based, meaning only the authenticated user specified by `{userId}` can access their own documents.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the document.

params.name: documentId
params.description: The unique identifier of the uploaded document.

definition.description: Stores private AI-generated content linked to a specific user's document. This data is only accessible by the owner specified by `{userId}`. Includes denormalized 'documentId' for integrity.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the AI result.

params.name: documentId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent document from which this AI result was generated.

params.name: aiResultId
params.description: The unique identifier for the specific AI-generated result.

definition.description: Stores publicly shareable AI results, accessible by a unique `shareSlug`. This collection provides read-only public access. Each document explicitly includes denormalized 'toolName', 'generatedContent', and 'isPubliclyShareable: true' for Authorization Independence and direct display. The `shareSlug` is used as the document ID for SEO-friendly URLs.

params.name: shareSlug
params.description: A unique, SEO-friendly slug used as the document ID for public access to the AI result.

firestore.reasoning:
The proposed Firestore structure prioritizes **Authorization Independence** and **Structural Segregation** to achieve secure, scalable, and debuggable security rules for the 'Share Result' feature. User-owned data, such as `Documents` and their corresponding private `AIResults`, are strictly segregated within a user's private path (`/users/{userId}/...`). This ensures that only the authenticated user (`request.auth.uid`) can access their own private data, simplifying security rules to path-based ownership checks.

For the 'Share Result' feature, a new top-level collection, `/public_ai_results`, is introduced. When a user chooses to share an AI result, a *copy* of the relevant `AIResult` data (including `toolName` and `generatedContent`) is denormalized and stored in this public collection. The `shareSlug` generated for public access is used as the document ID in `/public_ai_results/{shareSlug}`, making URLs SEO-friendly and enabling direct, efficient access. Each document in this public collection explicitly contains `isPubliclyShareable: true`, which serves as a clear invariant for public read access, eliminating the need for complex `get()` calls in security rules. This denormalization strategy ensures **Authorization Independence** because all necessary display information and authorization flags are present directly within the public `AIResult` document itself.

This segregation and denormalization also directly supports **Query Ability Patterns (QAPs)**. For private data, queries are naturally scoped by the user's path (e.g., listing all documents for `/users/{userId}/documents`). For public data, direct access via the `shareSlug` (`/public_ai_results/{shareSlug}`) is a simple and efficient read operation. There is no need for client-side filtering after fetching data, as the structural segregation guarantees that all documents in `/public_ai_results` are indeed public. Rules for public results become trivial (`allow read: if true;`), as the very existence of a document in that collection implies its public nature, further reinforced by the `isPubliclyShareable: true` field. This design avoids hierarchical authorization dependencies, making security rules robust and easy to debug.
